model.name: Dependency / Impact
model.purpose: Qualify every typed dependency or downstream-impact claim with the provenance, discovery method, authority, observation time, strength and claim-state metadata an agent needs to weigh the claim, without owning the edge itself, the evidence payload, or any verification, monitoring or adjudication process.
model.scope_statement: This partition is a frozen assertion mixin. It attaches to a dependency or impact assertion made in the core partition of WM-XCT-037 and answers: how the claim was established (declared, discovered, observed, inferred, attested), by which registered procedure and tool, on whose authority, against which retrievable evidence reference, with what stated confidence and reproducibility conditions, at which phenomenon/observation/ingestion times, over which applicable scope, how complete the enumeration is, and whether the claim is currently asserted, superseded, retracted or contradicted. Endpoints and evidence artifacts (scan reports, SBOM documents, telemetry traces, signed attestations) are owned by external models; this partition carries only references, digests, selectors and declared metadata.
in_scope: Epistemic mode of a dependency claim and the differing evidentiary force of declared, discovered, observed, inferred and attested claims
Discovery method identification by reference to a registered, versioned method profile (technique class, tool identity, configuration and rule-set version, declared limitations)
Attribution of a claim to an accountable agent, its role in the evidence chain, and the authority basis for the assertion
Evidence source locators, content digests and in-document selectors binding a claim to a retrievable fragment without copying the payload
Confidence on a declared scale, stated uncertainty, repeatability/reproducibility conditions and the applicability envelope of the claim
Observation event record, phenomenon time versus observation (result) time versus ingestion time, declared validity window and freshness mechanism
Completeness and known-unknown declarations for an enumerated dependency scope, including the default 'incomplete' reading
Registration of contradiction, supersession and retraction states with reason, effective time and preserved superseded records
out_of_scope: Edge typing, direction, weight and downstream impact propagation, which belong to the core dependency/impact partition
Identity, classification and lifecycle of the endpoints a dependency edge connects
Storage, versioning, retention or deletion of evidence payloads (scan reports, SBOM files, traces, envelopes)
Cryptographic signature verification, trust-anchor management and attestation appraisal, which are Verifier-side functions under RFC 9334
Execution of scanners, monitors, instrumentation or telemetry pipelines, and any scheduling of re-observation
Adjudication of which contradictory claim is true, trust ranking of authorities, and any policy verdict or enforcement action
Audit-trail records and access-log storage, which belong to the adopting Dimension's audit model
Vulnerability, licence and copyright evidence, which are adjacent split areas

boundary_notes.neighbor: Core typed dependency and impact partition of WM-XCT-037
boundary_notes.distinction: The core partition owns the edge: its type, direction, conditionality and impact propagation. This partition owns only statements about how an edge claim came to be believed. A claim record without a resolvable edge reference is invalid here; an edge without evidence metadata is valid there.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Evidence artifact repository or document store
boundary_notes.distinction: Evidence artifacts are external entities addressed by locator plus content digest plus fragment selector, mirroring in-toto ResourceDescriptor and CycloneDX occurrence semantics. This partition never stores or mirrors payload bytes, never versions the artifact, and never schedules its deletion; it only marks a reference resolvable, unresolvable or digest-mismatched.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Attestation appraisal service (RFC 9334 Verifier and appraisal policy)
boundary_notes.distinction: RFC 9334 separates the producer of Evidence from the Verifier that appraises it against Appraisal Policy and Reference Values. This partition records Evidence-side facts and freshness inputs only; verdicts, Attestation Results, policy evaluation and enforcement are owned by the referenced appraisal service and must not be reproduced here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Adopting Dimension audit, retention and disposition models
boundary_notes.distinction: Claim-state transitions recorded here are subject-matter statements, not audit records. Access events, tamper-evident logs, legal hold and erasure execution are owned externally; this partition stores the disposition instruction reference and the resulting tombstone only.

A method profile describes a procedure the way sosa:usedProcedure does - as a referenced, reusable description - not as executable configuration. This partition cannot run, tune or schedule a detector, and holds no scanner state.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Data quality assessment and scoring services
boundary_notes.distinction: DQV quality measurements and metrics may be referenced as external annotations. This partition records the confidence a producer asserted and the conditions under which it was obtained; it does not compute quality scores, thresholds or rankings.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative vocabulary for Entity/Activity/Agent, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, qualifiedAttribution, hadPrimarySource, wasRevisionOf, generatedAtTime, wasInvalidatedBy and invalidatedAtTime - the backbone for claim provenance, derivation and retraction without deletion.

sources.title: Semantic Sensor Network Ontology (SOSA/SSN)
sources.organization: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) and Open Geospatial Consortium
sources.relevance: Defines Observation, FeatureOfInterest, madeBySensor, usedProcedure, Sampling, and the normative distinction between phenomenonTime (when the result applies to the feature) and resultTime (when the observation completed) - the basis for separating relation time from observation time.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary (DQV)
sources.relevance: Supplies QualityMeasurement, Metric, Dimension, QualityAnnotation and QualityCertificate, including value-plus-unit measurement structure and the precision dimension - used for referencing external quality assertions rather than computing them here.

sources.title: RFC 9334: Remote ATtestation procedureS (RATS) Architecture
sources.relevance: Separates Attester, Endorser, Reference Value Provider, Verifier and Relying Party, and defines Evidence, Endorsements, Reference Values, Attestation Results and Appraisal Policies plus nonce-, epoch-ID- and timestamp-based freshness - the normative basis for the authority roles, freshness mechanisms and the appraisal boundary.

sources.title: in-toto Attestation Framework - Statement layer, v1
sources.relevance: Envelope/statement/predicate layering, subject as ResourceDescriptor matched purely by digest, and predicateType typing - the model for binding a claim to an immutable subject by content digest and for keeping signed envelopes external.

sources.title: CycloneDX Bill of Materials JSON Schema, version 1.6 (bom-1.6.schema.json)
sources.relevance: Defines componentEvidence (identity field, confidence, concludedValue, methods with technique and per-method confidence, tools; occurrences with location/line/offset/symbol; callstack), the analysis technique enumeration (source-code-analysis, binary-analysis, manifest-analysis, ast-fingerprint, hash-comparison, instrumentation, dynamic-analysis, filename, attestation, other), the compositions aggregate enumeration including unknown and not-specified, and dependency ref/dependsOn/provides.

sources.title: SPDX Specification v3.0.1 - Core model, Relationship class
sources.relevance: Relationship carries from, to, relationshipType, completeness, startTime and endTime, and distinguishes NoneElement (asserting no relationships exist) from NoAssertionElement (no assertion made) - primary support for relation validity time and for explicit unknown states.

sources.title: SPDX Specification v3.0.1 - Core vocabulary, RelationshipCompleteness
sources.relevance: Normative three-value completeness vocabulary: complete (known to be exhaustive), incomplete (known not to be exhaustive), noAssertion (no assertion can be made) - the controlled vocabulary for completeness declarations.

sources.title: SPDX Specification v2.3 - Relationships between SPDX elements
sources.relevance: Defines DEPENDS_ON, DEPENDENCY_OF (explicitly stated as a dependency in machine-readable files), BUILD/DEV/OPTIONAL/PROVIDED/RUNTIME/TEST_DEPENDENCY_OF, STATIC_LINK/DYNAMIC_LINK, NOASSERTION handling and the relationship comment - evidence that manifest-declared dependency claims are a distinct, named category.

sources.title: OpenVEX Specification
sources.relevance: Document @id IRI, author, role, timestamp, version and last_updated; statements as a sequence in which later statements override and enrich earlier ones; mandatory justification or impact_statement for a not_affected status - the working precedent for supersession, required reasons and preserved prior assertions.

sources.title: International vocabulary of metrology - Basic and general concepts and associated terms (VIM), entry 2.26 measurement uncertainty
sources.organization: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology (JCGM) / BIPM
sources.relevance: Defines measurement uncertainty as a non-negative parameter characterizing the dispersion of values attributed to a measurand based on the information used, and links to repeatability condition (2.20), reproducibility condition (2.24) and metrological traceability (2.41) - the standard for stating strength and reproducibility limits rather than bare scores.

sources.title: Framing Software Component Transparency: Establishing a Common Software Bill of Materials (SBOM), third edition
sources.relevance: Public-authority framing of SBOM attributes including author, timestamp and dependency relationship, the requirement to identify known unknowns explicitly where the full dependency graph is not enumerated, and depth maturity levels (minimum expected direct dependencies, recommended further levels, aspirational full transitive closure).

bundles.name: Claim provenance, authority and evidentiary strength
bundles.description: Everything that establishes where a dependency or impact claim came from and how much weight it can carry: the epistemic mode, the registered procedure that produced it, the accountable agent and authority basis, the binding to retrievable evidence, and the declared confidence, uncertainty and applicability limits.
bundles.rationale: Standards that carry dependency assertions consistently separate the assertion from its warrant: CycloneDX records identity evidence with techniques, per-method confidence and occurrence locations; in-toto binds a predicate to a digest-identified subject inside a signed envelope; RFC 9334 separates Evidence producers from appraisal; PROV-O supplies attribution and derivation. Grouping these into one bundle keeps warrant metadata cohesive and keeps it out of the core edge model.

layers.name: Claim origin and discovery method
layers.description: How the claim was established and by which described procedure, distinguishing manifest-declared statements from static discovery, runtime observation, heuristic inference and third-party attestation.

findings.name: Epistemic mode and evidentiary force of a dependency claim
findings.description: Classifies how a dependency or impact claim was established - declared in a manifest or by a supplier, discovered by static inspection of source or binaries, observed in a running or instrumented system, inferred by similarity or heuristic, or attested by a signed third-party statement - and fixes that each mode carries different evidentiary force. CycloneDX separates manifest-analysis from binary-analysis, instrumentation, dynamic-analysis, ast-fingerprint, hash-comparison and attestation; SPDX names DEPENDENCY_OF specifically for dependencies explicitly stated in machine-readable files; RFC 9334 separates Evidence from Endorsements; PROV separates direct-knowledge sources (hadPrimarySource) from derivations. The mode is recorded, never re-derived, and never used here to decide which of several claims is correct.

questions.text: Which epistemic mode established this dependency claim - declared, discovered, observed, inferred or attested?
answer_data: Epistemic mode code from the governed mode vocabulary
Vocabulary identifier and pinned version
Reference to the external technique or relationship term the mode was mapped from

questions.text: What evidentiary force does the recorded mode carry, and which modes must never be silently merged into one edge claim?
answer_data: Declared force rank or ordering statement for the mode vocabulary
Merge-prohibition rule set (for example inferred claims may not be folded into declared claims)
Justification text where a mode of lower force is used as sole support

questions.text: How is an edge supported by several modes at once represented without collapsing their distinct force?
answer_data: One claim record per mode, each with its own method profile and strength
Sibling-claim grouping reference for the same edge
Flag marking whether modes agree, differ in scope or conflict

questions.text: When the mode is inferred or restated, which prior claim or source claim was it derived from?
answer_data: Derived-from claim references (PROV wasDerivedFrom)
Primary-source indicator distinguishing direct knowledge from restatement
Inference rule or similarity basis identifier

questions.text: Does this record assert direct knowledge of the dependency or a secondary restatement of another party's assertion?
answer_data: Primary-source boolean (PROV hadPrimarySource semantics)
Upstream publisher reference where the claim is a restatement
Restatement fidelity note (verbatim, mapped, summarised)

data_elements.name: Epistemic mode code
data_elements.description: Coded mode of establishment for the claim: declared, discovered, observed, inferred or attested.

data_elements.name: Mode vocabulary version pin
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the governed vocabulary the mode code is drawn from, so historic claims remain interpretable after vocabulary change.

data_elements.name: Primary-source indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the asserting agent had direct knowledge of the dependency or is restating another party's claim, following PROV hadPrimarySource.

data_elements.name: Derived-from claim reference
data_elements.description: Reference to one or more upstream claim records this claim was derived from or restates.

data_elements.name: Mode assignment rationale
data_elements.description: Short free text recording why the mode was assigned when the mapping from an external technique term is not one-to-one.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The epistemic mode is a small set of coded attributes carried on the claim record itself, together with references to upstream claims. Every cited standard expresses it as a field on an existing assertion (a CycloneDX technique value, an SPDX relationship type, a PROV property), never as a separate document. Minting an artifact here would create a parallel record of the claim and invite drift from the claim it qualifies.

findings.name: Discovery method, procedure and tool identification
findings.description: Identifies the reusable procedure that produced a claim by reference to a registered, versioned method profile: analysis technique class, tool identity and version, configuration or rule-set version, reference-data version, and the method's declared blind spots. This mirrors sosa:usedProcedure (a described, reusable procedure rather than an executing system), the CycloneDX technique and tools structure, and the DQV notion of a metric as a defined procedure. The profile is descriptive metadata; this partition never executes, schedules or configures a detector.

questions.text: Which registered method profile and version produced this claim?
answer_data: Method profile identifier and semantic version
Configuration digest in force for the producing run
Reference to the profile registration record

questions.text: Which analysis technique class does the method belong to and what are its documented blind spots?
answer_data: Technique class code aligned to the CycloneDX technique enumeration
Declared limitation statements (for example dynamic linking not visible to manifest analysis)
Known false-positive and false-negative modes recorded as text

questions.text: What rule-set, signature database or reference-data version was in force when the method ran?
answer_data: Rule-set or reference-data identifier and version
Reference values or baseline set reference
Digest of the effective configuration bundle

questions.text: Which changes to a method profile require existing claims to be re-derived rather than merely reinterpreted?
answer_data: Profile change classification (editorial, additive, semantic-breaking)
Re-derivation requirement flag per change class
Superseded profile version reference retained for historic claims

data_elements.name: Method profile reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the registered method profile version that produced the claim.

data_elements.name: Analysis technique code
data_elements.description: Technique class of the method, aligned to the CycloneDX technique enumeration (source-code-analysis, binary-analysis, manifest-analysis, ast-fingerprint, hash-comparison, instrumentation, dynamic-analysis, filename, attestation, other).

data_elements.name: Tool identity record
data_elements.description: Structured identity of each tool involved: name, publisher, version and, where available, tool binary digest.

data_elements.name: Rule-set or reference-data version
data_elements.description: Version of the rules, signatures or reference values applied during the producing run.

data_elements.name: Declared method limitation
data_elements.description: Documented blind spot or systematic limitation of the method, carried so downstream consumers do not read absence of a claim as absence of a dependency.

artifacts.name: Method profile descriptor
artifacts.description: A versioned, citable descriptor of one detection or declaration procedure: technique class, tool identity set, configuration and rule-set version pins, applicable subject classes, declared limitations and the confidence scale it emits. Claims reference the descriptor rather than restating the procedure, and the descriptor holds no executable configuration and no scan results.
media_or_form: citable reference entry in a Dimension-governed method registry
artifacts.identity_strategy: Dimension-governed method-profile identifier plus semantic version, with a configuration digest as content identity; superseded versions are retained and referenced by historic claims.

layers.name: Attribution, authority and evidence binding
layers.description: Who stands behind a claim, on what authority, and how the claim is bound to a retrievable piece of external evidence without importing the evidence itself.

findings.name: Asserting agent, role and authority basis
findings.description: Records the accountable agent for a claim, its role in the evidence chain and the basis of its authority. PROV-O supplies wasAttributedTo and qualifiedAttribution; RFC 9334 distinguishes Attester (produces Evidence), Endorser (vouches for capability), Reference Value Provider and Verifier; OpenVEX requires an author and permits a role and supplier; CISA lists the author of SBOM data as a required attribute. The agent record distinguishes the party that observed from the party that published, and names the authority basis (supplier of record, delegated, self-asserted, third-party). Signature verification and trust decisions about the agent are external.

questions.text: Which agent is accountable for this claim and in what role within the evidence chain?
answer_data: Agent reference resolved in the external party registry
Role code aligned to attester, endorser, reference-value provider, tool or reviewer
Qualified attribution record carrying role plus time of attribution

questions.text: On what authority basis is the claim made - supplier of record, delegated authority, self-assertion or third-party assertion?
answer_data: Authority basis code
Delegation reference or mandate identifier where authority is delegated
Scope of the authority (which subjects or product lines it covers)

questions.text: Which signed envelope or attestation carries this claim, and where is its signature verified?
answer_data: Attestation envelope or statement reference with predicate type
Signer key or identity reference as recorded by the producer
Named external verification service that owns signature and trust-anchor evaluation

questions.text: How are the agent that observed and the agent that published the claim kept distinguishable?
answer_data: Separate observing-agent and publishing-agent references
On-behalf-of / delegation chain reference
Indicator that observation and publication were performed by the same agent

data_elements.name: Asserting agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent accountable for the claim, resolved in the external party or agent registry.

data_elements.name: Evidence-chain role code
data_elements.description: Role of the agent in the evidence chain, aligned to RATS roles and to tool/reviewer roles.

data_elements.name: Authority basis code
data_elements.description: Coded basis for the agent's standing to make the claim: supplier of record, delegated, self-asserted or third-party.

data_elements.name: Observing agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent or system that actually made the observation, where different from the publisher.

data_elements.name: Attestation envelope reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the external signed envelope or statement carrying the claim, with its predicate type; the envelope body is not stored here.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Attribution is pure reference data: pointers into an externally owned party registry plus coded role and authority values on the claim. The signed envelope that would be the natural artifact is created, versioned and verified outside this partition under in-toto or equivalent rules, so declaring a local artifact would duplicate an externally owned record and imply ownership of signature semantics this partition explicitly disclaims.

findings.name: Evidence source locator, fragment selector and payload exclusion
findings.description: Binds a claim to the specific external evidence that supports it: a resolvable locator, a content digest that pins the exact revision, a fragment selector (file path, line, byte offset, symbol, call-stack frame, statement identifier), the media type, and any retrieval constraint. In-toto matches subjects purely by digest; CycloneDX occurrences carry location, line, offset and symbol; OpenVEX documents carry an IRI @id. The invariant is that no payload bytes, extracted secrets or excerpt text beyond a minimal locating selector are copied into this model, and that a broken or mismatched reference degrades the claim's resolvability without rewriting history.

questions.text: How is the supporting evidence located again later, and which identifier pins the exact revision that was seen?
answer_data: Resolvable locator (URI or system-of-record reference)
Content digest with named algorithm
Retrieval hints such as media type, repository or snapshot reference

questions.text: Which fragment of the evidence actually supports the claim?
answer_data: Selector structure: path, line, byte offset, symbol or call-stack frame
Statement or record identifier inside a structured evidence document
Selector syntax identifier and version

questions.text: What must never be copied out of the evidence payload into this model?
answer_data: Payload-exclusion rule set (no source excerpts, no credentials, no personal data, no full documents)
Maximum permitted selector granularity
Escalation path when a locator alone is insufficient to support the claim

questions.text: What happens to a claim when its evidence reference becomes unresolvable or its digest no longer matches?
answer_data: Reference resolvability state code (resolvable, unresolvable, digest-mismatch)
Time the resolvability state was last checked and by whom
Rule that resolvability state never alters the historic claim record and never triggers deletion

data_elements.name: Evidence locator
data_elements.description: Resolvable identifier of the external evidence entity supporting the claim.

data_elements.name: Evidence content digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the referenced evidence with named algorithm, pinning the revision that was actually seen.

data_elements.name: Evidence fragment selector
data_elements.description: Structured pointer to the supporting fragment: path, line, offset, symbol, call-stack frame or statement identifier.

data_elements.name: Evidence media type
data_elements.description: Media type or format identifier of the referenced evidence, used to select the correct selector syntax.

data_elements.name: Reference resolvability state
data_elements.description: Current state of the evidence reference: resolvable, unresolvable or digest-mismatch, with the time of the last resolution attempt.

data_elements.name: No-evidence rationale
data_elements.description: Mandatory explanation when a claim is recorded with no evidence reference at all, so that unsupported claims stay visibly unsupported.

artifacts.name: Evidence reference manifest
artifacts.description: A serialised set of locator, digest, selector and media-type rows for one claim set or observation run, listing where the supporting evidence lives and which fragments were relied on. It is a reference index only: it contains no payload bytes, no excerpts beyond selectors, and it neither versions nor retains the evidence it points at.
media_or_form: attachment to a claim-set transfer package
artifacts.identity_strategy: Manifest identifier scoped to the claim set or observation run, plus a monotonic sequence number and the manifest's own content digest; each row is keyed by evidence locator plus digest.

layers.name: Evidentiary strength, uncertainty and applicability limits
layers.description: How strongly a claim is asserted, under what measurement conditions, and how far the claim may legitimately be generalised.

findings.name: Confidence, uncertainty, applicable scope and reproducibility conditions
findings.description: Captures the strength a producer asserted and the conditions that bound it. CycloneDX carries a confidence value on an identity conclusion and on each contributing method; VIM defines measurement uncertainty as a non-negative parameter characterising the dispersion of values attributed to a measurand based on the information used, and distinguishes repeatability from reproducibility conditions; DQV structures a measurement as a value against a defined metric. This finding requires the scale to be named and versioned, the conditions under which the result was obtained to be stated, the applicability envelope (platform, build profile, configuration, population) to be declared, and comparability across methods to be governed by an explicit rule. It records these values; it never computes a score, threshold or verdict.

questions.text: On which named scale is confidence expressed and what exactly does its value denote?
answer_data: Confidence value plus scale identifier and version
Scale definition: range, ordering, whether values are probabilities, ordinal ranks or opaque tool scores
Per-method confidence values where several methods contributed

questions.text: Under which repeatability, intermediate precision or reproducibility conditions was the result obtained?
answer_data: Condition class code (repeatability, intermediate, reproducibility)
Statement of what was held constant and what varied (operator, tool version, environment, time)
Uncertainty statement or dispersion parameter where the producer supplied one

questions.text: To which configurations, platforms or build profiles does this claim apply, and where does it stop applying?
answer_data: Applicability envelope: platform, architecture, build profile, feature flags, deployment class
Explicit non-applicability exclusions
Rule that a claim outside its envelope is unsupported rather than false

questions.text: May confidence values produced by different methods be compared or aggregated, and under what recorded rule?
answer_data: Comparability rule identifier or an explicit not-comparable declaration
Mapping table reference between scales where one exists
Prohibition on arithmetic across unmapped scales

questions.text: What remains unknowable from this method even at its maximum stated confidence?
answer_data: Method ceiling statement inherited from the method profile limitations
Distinction between not-detected and not-present
Recommended corroborating mode for claims at the ceiling

data_elements.name: Confidence value
data_elements.description: Producer-asserted confidence for the claim, meaningless without its scale reference.

data_elements.name: Confidence scale reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the scale that defines the confidence value's range, ordering and interpretation; mandatory whenever a confidence value is present.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty statement
data_elements.description: Dispersion parameter or qualitative uncertainty statement supplied by the producer, following the VIM notion of uncertainty based on the information used.

data_elements.name: Measurement condition class
data_elements.description: Whether the result was obtained under repeatability, intermediate precision or reproducibility conditions.

data_elements.name: Applicability envelope
data_elements.description: Structured statement of the configurations, platforms, build profiles or populations to which the claim applies, with explicit exclusions.

data_elements.name: Comparability rule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the recorded rule permitting or forbidding comparison and aggregation of this confidence value with values from other scales.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Strength values are attributes of an individual claim and are only meaningful attached to it; the reusable part - the scale definition and the method's limitations - already lives in the governed confidence-scale vocabulary and in the method profile descriptor declared elsewhere in this model. Emitting a separate strength document would either duplicate those registered definitions or create a scoring record that edges toward the assessment role this partition disclaims.

bundles.name: Observation record, currency and claim-state resolution
bundles.description: The observation event that produced a claim, the several distinct times attached to it, the declared window in which the claim remains assertable, and the resolution states a claim can occupy: complete or unknown enumeration, contradicted, superseded or retracted.
bundles.rationale: SOSA separates phenomenon time from result time, SPDX 3.0.1 gives a relationship its own start and end time, and RFC 9334 treats freshness as an explicit property demonstrated by timestamp, nonce or epoch identifier. Separately, SPDX RelationshipCompleteness, CycloneDX compositions aggregate and CISA's known-unknowns requirement all show that unknown enumeration must be stated rather than inferred, while OpenVEX and PROV invalidation show that assertions are superseded and retracted rather than deleted. These concerns share one lifecycle and belong in one bundle.

layers.name: Observation event and time semantics
layers.description: The discrete observation or assertion event, its subject binding and environment, and the several times that must be kept apart.

findings.name: Observation event, subject binding and environment
findings.description: Records the discrete act that produced a claim, following the SOSA pattern of an Observation carried out by a procedure on a feature of interest. Here the feature of interest is the dependency edge or the artifact under inspection, referenced - never redefined - through the core partition and external endpoint registries. The record captures the environment instance in which the observation was made (build run, deployment, target environment, as RFC 9334 separates Target from Attesting Environment), the run grouping that keeps sibling claims from one execution linked, and whether the whole population or a sample was inspected.

questions.text: Which dependency edge or endpoint was the subject of this observation, and how is that subject referenced?
answer_data: Reference to the edge claim in the core dependency partition
Endpoint references resolved in external registries, including subject digest where the subject is an artifact
Feature-of-interest kind (edge, source endpoint, target endpoint, package archive)

questions.text: In which environment instance, build run or deployment was the observation made?
answer_data: Environment instance reference (build identifier, cluster, host class, target environment)
Environment kind code distinguishing build-time, test, staging and production
Note on how representative the environment is of the environment the claim will be used for

questions.text: Was the whole population inspected or only a sample, and how was that sample selected?
answer_data: Coverage basis: exhaustive, sampled or opportunistic
Sampling method and selection criteria
Observed population size and inspected count where known

questions.text: Which observation run does this record belong to so that all claims from one execution stay linked?
answer_data: Observation run identifier
Procedure run reference linking to the method profile version used
Count and list reference of sibling claims produced by the same run

data_elements.name: Observation event identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the discrete observation or assertion act that produced the claim.

data_elements.name: Subject edge reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the dependency or impact edge claim being qualified; the edge itself is owned by the core partition.

data_elements.name: Environment instance reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the build run, deployment or target environment in which the observation was made.

data_elements.name: Observation run reference
data_elements.description: Grouping reference tying all claims produced by one execution of a method profile together.

data_elements.name: Coverage basis
data_elements.description: Whether the observation was exhaustive over its scope, sampled or opportunistic, with the sampling method where applicable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The observation event is a structured record on the claim graph consisting of identifiers and references to externally owned environments, runs and subjects. Materialising it as an artifact would create a second copy of scanner or pipeline run records that the producing system already owns, which conflicts with the rule that this partition is not a monitoring or scanning system and holds no execution state.

findings.name: Time model and freshness inputs
findings.description: Keeps four kinds of time distinct: the time the asserted dependency relation actually held (SPDX 3.0.1 relationship startTime and endTime; SOSA phenomenonTime), the time the observation completed (SOSA resultTime), the time the claim was recorded in this model (ingestion), and the declared validity boundary after which the claim should be re-observed. It also records which freshness mechanism demonstrates recency of the underlying evidence - signed timestamp, nonce or epoch identifier, as enumerated by RFC 9334 - and notes RFC 9334's warning that claim values may have been generated long before they were signed. This finding supplies freshness inputs; whether a claim is too stale to rely on is decided by an external appraisal or policy service.

questions.text: When did the asserted dependency relation actually hold, as distinct from when it was observed?
answer_data: Relation start time and end time as RFC 3339 values with offset
Phenomenon time or interval where the relation is instantaneous
Indicator that relation time is unknown rather than open-ended

questions.text: When was the observation completed and when was the resulting claim recorded here?
answer_data: Observation result time
Ingestion time recorded by this model
Producer-asserted publication time where the producing document carries one

questions.text: For how long does this claim remain assertable before it must be re-observed?
answer_data: Declared validity boundary or maximum age
Basis for the boundary (method profile default, producer declaration, subject volatility)
Behaviour after the boundary: still readable, marked stale, never auto-deleted

questions.text: By which mechanism is the recency of the underlying evidence demonstrated - signed timestamp, nonce or epoch identifier?
answer_data: Freshness mechanism code (timestamp, nonce, epoch identifier, none)
Challenge value or epoch identifier reference where one was used
Note on clock trust and possible lag between value generation and signing

data_elements.name: Relation start time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time from which the asserted dependency relation is stated to hold.

data_elements.name: Relation end time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time after which the asserted dependency relation is stated no longer to hold.

data_elements.name: Observation result time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time at which the observation or assertion act completed, following sosa:resultTime.

data_elements.name: Ingestion time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time at which this model recorded the claim, always stored separately from observation time.

data_elements.name: Declared validity boundary
data_elements.description: Time or maximum age after which the claim should be re-observed before further reliance.

data_elements.name: Freshness mechanism code
data_elements.description: Mechanism used to demonstrate recency of the underlying evidence: timestamp, nonce, epoch identifier or none.

data_elements.name: Freshness challenge reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the nonce or epoch identifier that was incorporated by the producer, without reproducing the challenge protocol.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are timestamp fields and one coded mechanism value on the claim record. No cited standard produces a separate time document, and any derived age figure is a read-only projection over fields already stored; publishing it as an artifact would imply an acceptability judgement that belongs to the external appraisal service.

layers.name: Unknowns, contradiction, supersession and retraction
layers.description: Explicit statements about what is not known, and the governed states a claim moves through when it is disputed, replaced or withdrawn.

findings.name: Completeness declarations and known unknowns
findings.description: Requires an explicit statement of whether an enumerated dependency set for a stated scope is exhaustive, known to be partial, or not asserted at all. SPDX 3.0.1 defines completeness as complete, incomplete or noAssertion, and distinguishes a NoneElement target (asserting no relationships exist) from a NoAssertionElement target (no assertion made); CycloneDX compositions carry an aggregate value including unknown and not-specified; CISA requires SBOM authors to identify known unknowns explicitly where the full dependency graph is not enumerated, and sets depth expectations from direct dependencies upward. The governing rule adopted here is that a missing completeness statement is read as incomplete, never as complete.

questions.text: Is the enumerated dependency set for this scope exhaustive, known to be partial, or not asserted at all?
answer_data: Completeness code aligned to complete, incomplete and noAssertion
External aggregate value where imported from a composition-style document
Agent and time of the completeness declaration

questions.text: How is 'this node has no further dependencies' distinguished from 'its dependencies are unknown'?
answer_data: Explicit no-further-dependencies assertion flag
Unknown-enumeration marker with reason code
Rule forbidding an empty dependency list from being read as either

questions.text: Which scope does the completeness statement cover - direct dependencies only, a stated depth, or the transitive closure?
answer_data: Scope reference (node, subgraph, product release)
Declared depth: direct only, n levels, transitive closure
Dependency classes included or excluded (build, dev, test, optional, provided, runtime)

questions.text: What is the default interpretation when no completeness statement is present at all?
answer_data: Recorded default rule: absent means incomplete
Warning or flag emitted to consumers on absent declarations
Migration rule for legacy records ingested without a declaration

data_elements.name: Completeness code
data_elements.description: Completeness of the enumerated dependency set for the stated scope: complete, incomplete or no-assertion.

data_elements.name: Completeness scope reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the node, subgraph or release the completeness statement covers.

data_elements.name: Declared enumeration depth
data_elements.description: Depth to which enumeration was attempted: direct dependencies only, a stated number of levels, or transitive closure.

data_elements.name: No-further-dependencies assertion
data_elements.description: Affirmative assertion that the subject has no further dependencies, distinct from an empty or absent enumeration.

data_elements.name: Unknown-enumeration reason code
data_elements.description: Why enumeration is incomplete or not asserted: method limitation, access restriction, supplier non-disclosure, opaque binary, not attempted.

data_elements.name: Included dependency classes
data_elements.description: Dependency classes the enumeration covered (build, development, test, optional, provided, runtime), so partial scope is not read as partial completeness.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A completeness declaration is a coded assertion scoped to a node or subgraph and carried with the claim set it qualifies. In the cited standards it is a field on a relationship or a composition, never a standalone document, and separating it into an artifact would let a graph and its completeness statement drift apart, which is the exact failure the known-unknowns requirement exists to prevent.

findings.name: Contradiction registration, supersession and retraction
findings.description: Governs the states a claim can occupy after assertion. Contradiction is registered as a pairwise relation between claims about the same edge whose scopes overlap but whose content disagrees; supersession follows the OpenVEX pattern where a later statement from the same authority overrides and enriches an earlier one; retraction follows PROV invalidation (wasInvalidatedBy, invalidatedAtTime), leaving the retracted record inspectable rather than deleted, with a required reason in the spirit of OpenVEX's mandatory justification. This partition registers and routes these states; it never decides which contradictory claim is true, and per RFC 9334 that appraisal belongs to the Verifier or an equivalent external adjudicator.

questions.text: When are two claims about the same edge genuinely contradictory rather than merely different in scope or time?
answer_data: Contradiction test: overlapping subject, overlapping applicability envelope, overlapping validity interval, incompatible assertion
Non-contradiction cases: disjoint envelopes, disjoint time intervals, different dependency classes
Recorded contradiction kind (existence, direction, class, completeness)

questions.text: Which claim supersedes which, and on what recorded basis does that ordering hold?
answer_data: Supersedes and superseded-by references
Ordering basis: same-authority document version, producer-asserted sequence, or explicit operator decision
Explicit not-ordered marker where the claims come from different authorities

questions.text: How is a retraction recorded so that the retracted claim remains inspectable afterwards?
answer_data: Claim state transition to retracted with invalidation time
Retained original claim record and its evidence references
Tombstone content rules where evidence-bearing fields are minimised

questions.text: Who may retract or supersede a claim, and what reason must accompany the action?
answer_data: Permitted actor set: original asserting agent, delegated steward, or authority named in the mandate
Mandatory reason code plus free-text justification
Rule that a third party may register a contradiction but may not retract another agent's claim

questions.text: Where is a registered contradiction sent for resolution, given that this partition does not adjudicate truth?
answer_data: Referral reference to the external appraisal, review or governance process
Referral state (open, referred, resolved-elsewhere) with no local verdict field
Back-reference recording the external outcome identifier only

data_elements.name: Claim state code
data_elements.description: Current state of the claim: asserted, superseded, retracted or contradicted.

data_elements.name: Supersedes claim reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the earlier claim or claims this record overrides, following the OpenVEX sequence pattern.

data_elements.name: State effective time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 time from which the supersession or retraction takes effect, recorded separately from the ingestion time of the state change.

data_elements.name: Retraction or supersession reason
data_elements.description: Mandatory coded reason with optional free text explaining why the claim was withdrawn or replaced.

data_elements.name: Contradiction pair reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the counterpart claim with which this claim is registered as contradictory, plus the contradiction kind.

data_elements.name: Adjudication referral reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the external review, appraisal or governance case handling the contradiction; carries no local verdict.

artifacts.name: Claim revision and retraction notice
artifacts.description: A dated, versioned notice that records supersession or retraction of one or more previously published claims: prior claim identifiers, new state, effective time, reason and issuing agent. Modelled on the OpenVEX document pattern of versioned statements that override earlier ones, it exists so that consumers who already received a claim can be told it changed. It contains no verdict on which claim is true and no audit record of who read it.
media_or_form: published change notice for downstream consumers
entry in a claim-set change feed
artifacts.identity_strategy: Notice identifier with a monotonically increasing version per issuing agent and claim scope, carrying the identifiers of every affected prior claim; sequence numbers are never reused after retraction.

functions.name: Record claim origin and epistemic mode
functions.description: Attach an epistemic mode, primary-source indicator and derivation references to a dependency or impact claim asserted in the core partition.
inputs: Reference to the edge claim being qualified
Epistemic mode code and vocabulary version pin
Optional derived-from claim references and mode rationale
outputs: Claim provenance record with mode, vocabulary pin and derivation links
Rejection with reason when the mode code is not in the pinned vocabulary
preconditions: The referenced edge claim resolves in the core partition
The mode vocabulary version is registered and not withdrawn
effects: Creates an immutable mode assignment on the claim
Makes the claim eligible for strength and completeness qualification
Does not alter the edge, its type or its impact propagation

functions.description: Create or supersede a method profile descriptor covering technique class, tool identity, configuration and rule-set version pins, applicable subject classes and declared limitations.

Configuration and rule-set version pins with configuration digest
Declared limitations, applicable subject classes and emitted confidence scale reference

preconditions: The technique class exists in the pinned technique vocabulary
The referenced confidence scale is registered
effects: Adds a citable, versioned procedure description that claims can reference
Retains superseded profile versions so historic claims stay interpretable
Does not execute, configure or schedule any detector

functions.name: Bind an evidence reference to a claim
functions.description: Attach one or more locator, digest, media-type and fragment-selector rows to a claim, or record an explicit no-evidence rationale, without importing any payload.
inputs: Claim reference
Evidence locator, optional content digest and media type
Fragment selector or explicit no-evidence rationale
outputs: Evidence reference rows attached to the claim
Evidence reference manifest entry for the claim set
Validation error when neither an evidence reference nor a no-evidence rationale is supplied

The selector syntax matches the declared media type

Enforces the payload-exclusion rule at write time
Does not fetch, cache, mirror, version or delete the referenced evidence

functions.name: Record an observation event and its times
functions.description: Record the observation act, its subject and environment, its coverage basis, and the distinct relation, result, ingestion and validity times together with the freshness mechanism used.
inputs: Subject edge and endpoint references, environment instance reference
Observation run reference, coverage and sampling basis
Relation start/end time, observation result time, declared validity boundary, freshness mechanism and challenge reference
outputs: Observation event record with all times stored in separate fields
Freshness descriptor exposing recorded times and the validity boundary for external policy evaluation

Observation result time is not later than ingestion time unless an explicit clock-skew note is supplied

Keeps relation time, observation time and ingestion time permanently distinguishable
Emits freshness inputs only and makes no acceptability or staleness decision

functions.name: Record confidence, conditions and applicability
functions.description: Record a producer-asserted confidence value against a named scale, the measurement condition class, any uncertainty statement, and the applicability envelope that bounds generalisation of the claim.
inputs: Claim reference and confidence value
Confidence scale reference and version, condition class code, uncertainty statement
Applicability envelope and exclusions

Rejection when a confidence value is supplied without a registered scale reference

The applicability envelope uses registered platform and profile vocabularies

Blocks cross-scale arithmetic unless a recorded comparability rule permits it
Computes no derived score, threshold or ranking

functions.name: Declare completeness or a known unknown
functions.description: Record whether an enumerated dependency set for a stated scope is complete, incomplete or not asserted, distinguishing an affirmative no-further-dependencies statement from unknown enumeration and naming the reason.
inputs: Scope reference, declared depth and included dependency classes
Completeness code and, where applicable, unknown reason code
Affirmative no-further-dependencies assertion where it applies

Consumer-facing warning where a scope has no declaration

The declaring agent has an authority basis for the scope

Applies the default rule that an absent declaration is read as incomplete

Overlap test result covering subject, envelope and time interval
Referral target reference

Not-contradictory determination with the disjoint dimension named

Both claims carry applicability envelopes and times sufficient to run the overlap test

Records a referral reference and referral state only

Effective time, reason code and justification text
Issuing agent reference and authority basis
outputs: Updated claim state with invalidation time and preserved original record
Claim revision and retraction notice for downstream consumers

A reason code is supplied; supersession additionally requires a recorded ordering basis
