Never performs a hard delete of the claim or its evidence references
Does not delete, alter or expire the external evidence the claim referenced

composition.target: WM-XCT-037 core partition: typed dependency edge and downstream impact propagation
composition.purpose: This partition attaches provenance, observation and claim-state qualification to edges asserted in the core partition. Edge typing, direction, conditionality, weighting and impact propagation remain entirely in the core; a record here is invalid without a resolvable edge reference.

composition.target: Endpoint subject registries (component, service, asset and system-of-record models)
composition.purpose: Claims cite endpoints by their authoritative identifiers, and artifacts additionally by content digest in the in-toto subject style. Endpoint identity, classification and lifecycle are not restated or maintained here.

composition.target: Evidence artifact repository or document store owned by the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Carries locator, digest, media type and fragment selector for supporting evidence. Payload storage, versioning, access control at the payload level, retention scheduling and deletion of evidence artifacts are owned by the repository; this partition only records reference resolvability state.

Map claim records to Entity, Activity and Agent, and map derivation, attribution, revision and invalidation to wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, qualifiedAttribution, wasRevisionOf, wasInvalidatedBy and invalidatedAtTime. Alignment is a recorded mapping with a version pin, not a conformance claim.
Map the observation event, feature of interest, used procedure, sampling and the phenomenonTime/resultTime distinction. Sensor and platform management remain outside this partition.

composition.target: Attestation appraisal service under RFC 9334 (Verifier, Appraisal Policy, Reference Values)
composition.purpose: Supplies Evidence-side references and freshness inputs to appraisal. Appraisal policy, Attestation Results, verdicts, trust-anchor management and any enforcement action are owned by the appraisal service and are explicitly not modelled here.

composition.target: SBOM, VEX and attestation interchange bindings (SPDX 3.0.1, CycloneDX 1.6, in-toto Statement v1, OpenVEX 0.2.0)
composition.purpose: Version-pinned field mappings for import and export of evidence metadata: technique and completeness vocabularies, occurrence selectors, subject digests, document identity and supersession sequences. Mappings are recorded with known lossy edges rather than asserted as conformance.

composition.target: Party and agent registry (organizations, tools, individuals) of the adopting Dimension
composition.purpose: Resolves asserting, observing and publishing agents and their delegation chains. Agent identity, credentialing and organisational lifecycle are owned by the registry.

composition.target: Adopting-Dimension retention, disposition and audit-record models
composition.purpose: Owns retention schedules, legal hold, erasure execution and audit-trail semantics. This partition records the disposition instruction reference and the resulting tombstone, and emits access and change events to the audit model without defining, storing or querying audit records.

composition.target: Governed vocabularies for epistemic mode, confidence scales and completeness codes
composition.purpose: Holds the registered code lists and scale definitions that give recorded codes and confidence values their meaning, with version pins so historic claims stay interpretable. Vocabulary governance and publication are owned by the registry, not by this partition.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must designate an owner for this partition who is distinct from the owner of the core dependency/impact partition only if the boundary between edge assertion and edge qualification is documented; otherwise a single owner holds both with the boundary recorded in the package.

The owner package must register the governed vocabularies this partition depends on - epistemic mode codes, technique classes, confidence scales, completeness codes, unknown reason codes and authority-basis codes - each with a resolvable identifier and version history.

The owner package must name the external services that own evidence payload storage, signature verification, appraisal, adjudication, retention execution and audit records, so that no consumer expects those functions here.

The owner package must state the default reading of an absent completeness declaration (incomplete) and the payload-exclusion rule, and must record any deviation as an explicit local policy exception.
dimension.namespace_guidance: All local identifiers are lower-kebab-case and prefixed dep-evd- within the WM-XCT-037 namespace. Codes drawn from external vocabularies keep their source token verbatim and carry a namespace prefix plus version pin (for example cyclonedx-1-6:manifest-analysis, spdx-3-0-1:noAssertion) rather than being renamed; locally minted codes must not reuse an external token with different meaning.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-xct-037 must record this partition's composition links and keep the review_state boundary-review-required until the core/qualification boundary is confirmed by the owner.
Method profiles, confidence scales and code lists must be registered as Dimension-governed registries with resolvable identifiers, version history and retention of superseded versions.
External alignment mappings (PROV-O, SOSA/SSN, DQV, SPDX, CycloneDX, in-toto, OpenVEX, RFC 9334 roles) must be registered as versioned mapping records that list known lossy edges.

canonicalization_rules: Serialise records with deterministic key ordering; codes are lower-kebab-case tokens carrying their vocabulary namespace and version pin.
Store every time value as RFC 3339 with seconds and the offset exactly as asserted by the producer, plus a UTC-normalised twin for comparison; never discard the original offset.
Digests are lowercase hexadecimal with an explicit algorithm prefix; a digest without a named algorithm is invalid.

Distinguish three empty states explicitly: field absent (nothing recorded), asserted-none (affirmatively no items), and no-assertion (unknown); no serialisation may collapse them into an empty collection.
Evidence references are canonicalised as locator plus algorithm-qualified digest plus selector; two references are the same reference only when all three match.
patch_rules: Evidence-bearing fields - epistemic mode, method profile reference, agent, evidence references, times, confidence and completeness - are append-only; a correction is a new claim version linked by a revision reference, never an in-place edit.
Recorded observation result time and ingestion time are immutable; a clock correction is recorded as an additional annotated time with a correction note, leaving the originals intact.
Retraction and supersession are state transitions carrying effective time and reason; they never remove the prior record from the graph.
Non-evidence-bearing metadata (labels, cross-links, presentation hints) may be patched in place with the patch author and time recorded on the record itself.
compatibility_rules: Adding a code to a governed vocabulary is a minor change; changing the meaning or range of an existing code or confidence scale is breaking and requires a new vocabulary or scale identifier.
Version pins on external vocabularies move only through an explicit re-alignment record that lists changed tokens and lossy edges; historic claims keep their original pin.
Making a previously optional field mandatory is breaking for producers and requires a migration rule for existing records, which must not fabricate values - unknown stays unknown.
Consumers must tolerate unknown additional fields and must not infer meaning from field order or from the absence of an optional field.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the claim or artifact - for example the attestation statement identifier, VEX document identifier or scan-run identifier minted by the producing system - recorded verbatim together with a reference to its issuing system.
Governed global identifier or IRI where the producing ecosystem defines one, including a content-addressed identity such as an algorithm-qualified subject digest for immutable artifacts.

UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when no master-system identifier and no governed global identifier exist, and recorded as locally minted so consumers do not mistake it for an upstream identity.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every time value is an RFC 3339 date-time with explicit seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; local civil times without an offset are rejected at ingestion. Event time (the interval in which the asserted dependency relation held) is stored separately from observation time (when the observation or assertion act completed) and from ingestion time (when this model recorded the claim), and all three are retained in distinct fields even when their values coincide. A date alone is never an identifier and never substitutes for an observation time.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts - method profile descriptors, evidence reference manifests and claim revision or retraction notices - are named <model-id>/<artifact-kind>/<scope-or-subject-id>/<zero-padded sequence>@<semantic-version>. The sequence is monotonic within its scope and issuing agent, is never reused after a retraction, and is never derived from a date.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every serial artifact carries its own algorithm-qualified content digest and repeats the digests of the evidence it references. On re-resolution, a digest mismatch sets the reference state to digest-mismatch and blocks reuse of that reference for new claims, but never rewrites, deletes or silently repairs the historic record. Cryptographic signature verification and trust-anchor evaluation are performed by the referenced external verification service, and its outcome is stored only as a reference.

policies: No evidence payload may be stored, mirrored or cached in this model. Only locators, algorithm-qualified digests, media types, fragment selectors and declared metadata are permitted; excerpt text beyond a minimal locating selector, credentials and personal data must never be copied in.

Every claim record must carry an epistemic mode, a method profile reference, an accountable agent, an observation result time and an ingestion time, and either at least one evidence reference or an explicit no-evidence rationale.

This model does not adjudicate conflicting claims, rank the trustworthiness of authorities, compute derived quality scores, or issue policy verdicts; it records inputs for external appraisal and routes contradictions by reference.
A missing completeness declaration is read as incomplete, and an empty dependency enumeration is never read as an assertion that no dependencies exist.
Claim records are not hard-deleted as a matter of routine operation; withdrawal is expressed as retraction or supersession with a reason and an effective time.

read: Resolve the full provenance set for an edge: all claims, their modes, method profiles, agents, evidence references, strengths, times and current states.
Filter claims by epistemic mode, technique class, authority basis, completeness code or claim state, for an endpoint, subgraph or release scope.
Project freshness descriptors (recorded times, declared validity boundary and derived age) for external policy evaluation, with no acceptability judgement attached.
Resolve an evidence reference to its locator and digest for external retrieval; this model returns the reference, never the payload.
create: Create a claim provenance record only against a resolvable edge claim, with mandatory mode, method profile reference, agent, observation result time and system-stamped ingestion time.
Create method profile descriptor versions, evidence reference manifest entries and completeness declarations under the authority basis recorded for the creating agent.
Reject creation where a confidence value lacks a registered scale reference, where an evidence reference lacks both digest and no-evidence rationale, or where a time lacks an explicit offset.
update: Non-evidence-bearing metadata may be updated in place with the patch author and time recorded.
Evidence-bearing fields are changed only by creating a new claim version linked to its predecessor by a revision reference.
Reference resolvability state may be refreshed by re-resolution, recording the check time and checking agent; refreshing never alters the original claim content.
Claim state transitions to superseded, retracted or contradicted are performed only through the dedicated functions, with reason and effective time.
delete: Routine deletion is prohibited: a claim is withdrawn by retraction or supersession and retained as an inspectable record with its invalidation time and reason, following PROV invalidation rather than erasure.

Where erasure is nevertheless required, the record is reduced to a tombstone retaining claim identifier, subject edge reference, claim state, effective time, reason code and the disposition instruction reference; evidence-bearing fields are minimised and the tombstone itself is never removed, so downstream references do not dangle.

Retention periods, legal hold, erasure lawfulness and execution scheduling are owned by the adopting Dimension's retention and disposition model; this partition executes no retention policy of its own and records only the instruction reference and the resulting tombstone.

Deletion or expiry of referenced evidence artifacts is owned exclusively by the external evidence repository; when an artifact disappears this partition marks the reference unresolvable and takes no further action.
Deletion of audit or access records relating to this model is owned by the adopting Dimension's audit model and is out of scope here.

roles.name: Partition steward
responsibilities: Own the boundary between edge assertion (core partition) and edge qualification (this partition) and keep it documented.
Approve changes to policies, default readings and payload-exclusion rules.
Maintain the register of external services that own verification, appraisal, adjudication, retention and audit.

roles.name: Method profile registrar
responsibilities: Register and version method profile descriptors with technique class, tool identity, configuration pins and declared limitations.
Classify profile changes and decide whether existing claims must be re-derived or may be reinterpreted.
Retain superseded profile versions so historic claims remain interpretable.

roles.name: Claim recorder (producing system or integration)
responsibilities: Submit claim provenance records with mandatory mode, method profile, agent, times and evidence references or a no-evidence rationale.
Preserve producer-asserted confidence values with their scale rather than rescaling them.
Declare completeness and known unknowns for every scope it enumerates.

roles.name: Evidence reference custodian
responsibilities: Re-resolve evidence locators and digests on a schedule set by the adopting Dimension and record resolvability state with check time.
Enforce the payload-exclusion rule at ingestion and reject records carrying excerpted payload content.
Coordinate with the external evidence repository on locator stability without acquiring any control over payload retention.

roles.name: Contradiction triage coordinator
responsibilities: Run the overlap test, register genuine contradictions and record the disjoint dimension where claims are not in fact contradictory.
Route contradiction pairs to the named external adjudicator and record the referral state.
Ensure no local verdict, trust ranking or precedence decision is stored in this partition.

roles.name: Vocabulary alignment maintainer
responsibilities: Maintain version-pinned mappings to PROV-O, SOSA/SSN, DQV, SPDX, CycloneDX, in-toto, OpenVEX and RFC 9334 role terms.
Record known lossy mapping edges and conflicts rather than asserting conformance.
Manage vocabulary version-pin moves through explicit re-alignment records.

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Read access is granted per scope to identified principals with a stated purpose; claim provenance is readable only to principals already entitled to see the underlying edge in the core partition, since the qualification metadata can reveal the existence of an endpoint relationship. Write access is limited to the role that owns the specific record kind, and no principal may write a claim state transition on another agent's claim without a recorded mandate.
exceptions: Evidence locators that resolve into restricted systems may be masked for principals lacking entitlement to the target system, while the digest and the existence of the reference remain visible so the claim stays falsifiable.

Claim revision and retraction notices are readable by every principal that previously received the affected claim, even where their read entitlement to other scopes has since been reduced, so that consumers are not left holding a withdrawn claim.
Method profile descriptors may be published more widely than the claims that cite them, but declared limitations must travel with them so a profile is never quoted without its blind spots.
Tombstones remain readable to principals entitled to the original scope so that dangling references can be explained without restoring erased content.
audit_requirements: Emit read and write events for claim provenance records, evidence references and claim state transitions to the adopting Dimension's audit model; this partition defines no audit record structure, stores no audit trail and provides no audit query surface.

Include in each emitted event the acting principal, the scope touched, the record identifier and an RFC 3339 timestamp with offset, so the external audit model can correlate without re-reading this model.
Record within this model only the reference to a disposition or access decision taken elsewhere, never the decision logic or its evaluation trace.

read_order: AGENTS.md - identify the model, its type as a mixin partition, and the five resolvable URLs before any other action.
Specification URL - read scope, in-scope and out-of-scope lists, and the boundary notes naming externally owned functions.
Boundary and exclusions URL - confirm which neighbouring models own evidence payloads, verification, appraisal, adjudication, retention and audit before attempting any write.
Storage type URL - read the projection in use (document store, graph, git-backed files, MCP surface) and the canonicalization rules that apply regardless of projection.
Interface URL - read the available read and write operations and the access scopes they require.
Processes URL - read the procedures for recording claims, binding evidence references, declaring completeness, registering contradictions and issuing supersession or retraction notices.

coverage.claim: This partition covers the evidence, provenance and observation semantics needed to qualify dependency and impact claims in WM-XCT-037, to the depth supported by the cited primary standards. It deliberately excludes edge typing and impact propagation, evidence payload storage, signature verification and appraisal, scanner or monitor execution, truth adjudication and audit-record semantics. No claim of conformance to any cited standard is made; alignments are recorded mappings with named lossy edges.

checklist.notes: Identity priority puts the producing system's master identifier first, then governed IRIs and content digests (in-toto subject-by-digest), then locally minted UUID/ULID. Observation runs, method profiles and notices each have their own identity strategy; no identifier is date-derived.

Claim states are asserted, superseded, retracted and contradicted, with supersession modelled on OpenVEX statement sequences and retraction on PROV invalidation. Method profile versioning carries an explicit re-derive-or-reinterpret classification.

Every record binds to an edge claim owned by the core partition and to externally registered endpoints and agents. Contradiction, supersession and derivation are modelled as typed references between claims, not as embedded copies.

Relation validity time (SPDX startTime/endTime, SOSA phenomenonTime), observation result time (SOSA resultTime), ingestion time and declared validity boundary are stored in separate fields, all RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset, plus RFC 9334 freshness mechanisms.
PROV-O attribution, derivation, primary-source and revision semantics are mapped onto claim origin, agent attribution and supersession; the observing agent is kept distinct from the publishing agent.
Accountable agent, evidence-chain role and authority basis are mandatory; six operating roles are defined, and every externally owned function is named in boundary notes and composition links.

Write-time validation covers vocabulary membership, scale-reference presence for confidence values, offset-bearing timestamps, evidence-reference-or-rationale, and digest re-resolution state. Cryptographic verification is explicitly delegated.

Deny-by-default with bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes, entitlement inherited from the underlying edge, plus exceptions for masked locators, retraction notices, published method profiles and tombstones.

Routine deletion is prohibited in favour of retraction with preserved history; erasure yields a minimal tombstone. Retention scheduling, legal hold and erasure execution are owned by the adopting Dimension's retention model, evidence-artifact deletion by the evidence repository.

Version-pinned alignments to PROV-O, SOSA/SSN, DQV, SPDX 2.3 and 3.0.1, CycloneDX 1.6, in-toto Statement v1, OpenVEX 0.2.0 and RFC 9334 roles, with lossy edges recorded as conflicts rather than smoothed over.

Confidence is preserved with its scale, and VIM supplies the vocabulary for uncertainty and repeatability/reproducibility conditions, but no primary standard bridges opaque tool confidence values (CycloneDX 0-1) to a metrological uncertainty statement. Cross-scale arithmetic is therefore blocked rather than defined.

SPDX RelationshipCompleteness, the NoneElement/NoAssertionElement distinction, CycloneDX aggregate unknown values and CISA's known-unknowns requirement support explicit unknown states and the default incomplete reading.

OpenVEX supersession is defined within one author's document sequence; no cited primary source defines precedence between contradictory claims from different authorities. Ordering across authorities is left explicitly not-ordered and routed to external adjudication.
Locator, digest, media type and selector only, enforced at write time, with a maximum selector granularity rule and an escalation path when a locator alone cannot support the claim.

Geographic location is not a property of a dependency claim. Environment locus is modelled as an environment instance reference (build run, deployment, target environment), not as geometry; jurisdictional constraints on evidence retrieval are noted as regional assumptions.

known_omissions: Signature validity, key management and trust-anchor policy, deliberately delegated to an external verification service.
Any propagation algebra, blast-radius calculation or criticality scoring for downstream impact, which belongs to the core partition.
Elicitation protocols for human expert judgement beyond recording the agent, role and a confidence scale.
Licence, copyright and vulnerability evidence, which are adjacent split areas of the wider provider pass.
A canonical crosswalk table between CycloneDX aggregate values and SPDX RelationshipCompleteness values, which is left to a registered mapping record because no lossless mapping exists.
Sampling theory for partial observation beyond recording the coverage basis and selection criteria.
Rate, scheduling and triggering rules for re-observation, which depend on the adopting Dimension's operational policy.
conflicts: CycloneDX expresses confidence as a bare 0-1 number per identity conclusion and per contributing method with no defined statistical meaning, whereas VIM requires uncertainty to be expressed as a dispersion parameter tied to stated conditions. The two are not interconvertible and are recorded side by side rather than merged.

SPDX 3.0.1 attaches completeness to an individual relationship (complete, incomplete, noAssertion) while CycloneDX attaches an aggregate to a composition scope with a richer enumeration including unknown and not-specified. Mapping noAssertion to either unknown or not-specified loses information, so both source values are retained.

OpenVEX orders statements by author document version and timestamp within a single author's stream; PROV wasRevisionOf carries no ordering guarantee. Cross-author ordering cannot be inferred from timestamps alone because of clock skew, so this partition records an explicit not-ordered marker instead.

SOSA phenomenonTime/resultTime and SPDX Relationship startTime/endTime describe different things: the first pair concerns the observation act, the second the validity of the asserted relation. Tools that map one onto the other silently lose the distinction, which is why four separate time fields are mandated here.

CISA and NTIA framing sets the default reading of unstated completeness to incomplete, while many producing tools omit completeness entirely and are read downstream as complete. This partition adopts the authority reading and emits a consumer-facing warning on absent declarations.

RFC 9334 assigns appraisal to the Verifier, while several SBOM toolchains embed verdicts directly in evidence documents. Imported verdicts are stored only as references to an external decision, never as native fields.
regional_assumptions: The SBOM attribute expectations cited come from US federal-procurement framing (CISA, third edition, October 2024); other regimes, including the EU Cyber Resilience Act, may require different minimum attributes and the adopting Dimension must map them.
RFC 3339 offsets are mandatory and local civil-time inputs are normalised at ingestion; producers in jurisdictions that publish local-time-only records will be rejected until they supply an offset.

Evidence locators may resolve into systems in other jurisdictions; retrieval and even locator visibility may be constrained by export-control, privacy or contractual rules of the adopting Dimension, which is why locator masking is an access exception.
Authority-basis codes assume a supplier-of-record concept that exists in commercial software supply chains but may have no counterpart for internally developed or public-sector-mandated components.
adversarial_checks: Does any finding or function evaluate, verify, enforce or adjudicate? Checked: the strength finding records values but computes no score; the contradiction function registers and refers but selects no winner; the freshness output exposes recorded times but makes no staleness decision; signature verification and appraisal are named as externally owned in boundary notes and composition links.

Does the model become an audit store? Checked: audit requirements only emit events to the external audit model, no audit record structure or query surface is defined, and audit deletion is explicitly out of scope.

Does the model become an evidence store? Checked: the two evidence-facing artifacts are a method profile descriptor and a reference manifest of locators, digests and selectors; a payload-exclusion policy is enforced at write time and repeated in the create and update rules.

Could an empty dependency list be misread as an assertion of no dependencies? Checked: three empty states are canonicalised separately, an affirmative no-further-dependencies flag exists, and the default reading of an absent completeness declaration is incomplete.

Could a low-force claim be laundered into a high-force one? Checked: modes are immutable per claim, one claim record is required per mode, merging inferred into declared claims is prohibited, and cross-scale confidence arithmetic is blocked absent a recorded comparability rule.

Does anything here duplicate the core partition? Checked: no edge type, direction, weight, conditionality or propagation field is declared; every record requires a reference to an edge owned by the core, and the mixin relation is marked required.

Are any structural nodes unsupported by primary sources? Checked: each finding cites at least three primary sources from at least two organisations; the two acknowledged gaps (confidence-to-uncertainty bridging and cross-authority precedence) are marked as gaps rather than presented as canonical.
